**Context resolved:**

- **The blocking predicate is confirmed, at file:line.** `scripts/step9c_baseline.py:1941-1942`
  — inside `_paired_collection_reason` (line 1921), precondition 1 of the #2024 carve-out is
  `if node.file in touched_set: return "file-in-branch-diff"`. Called from line 2381; the
  audit row is appended by `_paired_skip_to_new` (line 1907), which keeps the node in
  `ctx.new` (blocking). The docstring is explicit about the intent: *"a branch-touched file
  keeps today's NEW semantics: main's copy of it is not the thing that failed"* — an
  assumption a sibling-synced file violates, because in that case main's copy IS exactly
  what ran.

- **`touched_set` traces to the three-dot branch diff.** `step9c_baseline.py:2263` sets
  `touched_set = set(ctx.touched)`; `_selector_context` (line 1657) sets
  `touched = sel.compute_touched(base, wt)`; `select_step9c_tests.compute_touched`
  (line 1235-1262) runs `git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD`. So a sibling file whose
  content the Step 5a arm WROTE and COMMITTED on the branch is in `touched` by construction
  — the same list that sizes the selector's gate set. Both halves of the body's mechanism
  (carve-out disabled AND gate-set inflated) share one root: `compute_touched` treats
  "changed vs the merge-base" as "changed by the branch".

- **No production provenance channel exists today.** `grep -rn "sync workflow-surface specs
  from" --include=*.py scripts/ src/ tests/` matches ONLY prose-pin tests
  (`tests/test_step10d_guard3.py`, `tests/test_issue_skill_lint_family_sync.py`); no
  production reader parses the sync commit subject, and `.claude/cache/` holds no
  synced-path sidecar. The sibling arm's subject IS distinguishable
  (`tests/test_issue_skill_lint_family_sync.py:711/766/776` pin
  `"... (spec-freshness; sibling-issue files)"` vs the plain `"... (spec-freshness)"`), so
  candidate shape (a) is buildable — but it would be a NEW channel, not a read of an
  existing one. This is the single most plan-relevant finding: it removes "just read the
  existing provenance" from the option set.

- **A content-identity signal is available with no new channel, and is strictly stronger
  than provenance.** A sibling-synced path's content at branch HEAD equals `origin/main`'s
  CURRENT content; it enters the three-dot diff only because it differs from the older
  merge-base. So "branch content == base content" identifies the class directly, is
  independent of HOW the content arrived (sync arm, manual copy, revert), and cannot widen
  the carve-out into the hole acceptance criterion 2 guards against: a genuinely
  branch-authored regression differs from main by definition, so it stays branch-touched
  and still classifies `new`. The plan will weigh this against the body's three candidate
  shapes; recording it here so the planner inherits the option.

**Chosen fix:** a base-identity filter. A path whose content at branch `HEAD` is byte-identical
to its content at the `base` tip is not a branch change, so it must not count as branch-touched
at either the Step 9c selector or the compare's #2024 carve-out precondition 1. The Step 5a
sibling-file sync (#1972) manufactures exactly that class.

**Root cause verified at file:line** (not inferred from the body): `_paired_collection_reason`
(`step9c_baseline.py:1921`) returns `"file-in-branch-diff"` at line 1941-1942 for any node whose
file is in `touched_set`; `touched_set` (line 2263) traces through `_selector_context` (line 1657)
to `select_step9c_tests.compute_touched` (line 1235), the three-dot `<base>...HEAD` diff. Both
reported symptoms — the disabled carve-out and the 61→217 gate-set inflation — share that root.

**Why content-identity over the body's three candidate shapes:** shape (a) (record the synced
path set) would require BUILDING a provenance channel — verified during clarification that no
production code reads the sync-commit anchor and no `.claude/cache/` sidecar exists — and is
strictly weaker, going stale the moment a synced path is later branch-edited. Shape (b) (widen
the #2206/#2208 revert arm to run-time failures) would delete the freshness the sync exists to
provide and cannot fire until the full gate wall is already spent. Shape (c) (selector-only)
fixes inflation but not classification, since a sibling test can still be co-selected via the
invariant / glob-scan / import-map arms.

**Change set:** (1) filter `compute_touched` — candidates `three_dot − two_dot`, each excluded
only on verified blob-OID equality, with the excluded set reported as `base_identical_excluded`;

regression fixture (`tests/test_step9c_base_identity.py`) distinguishing criterion 1 from
